items.headline: FMRB executive order draft draws coordinated civil-society pushback
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday placed the Frontier Model Review Board executive order in interagency draft circulation with civil-society litigation risk flagged in the abstract. Today AI Policy Institute, R Street, Public Knowledge, and Lawyers for Civil Justice file a joint open letter to OSTP and the White House Counsel's office arguing that any pre-release notification regime relying on Defense Production Act Section 708 voluntary information-sharing without an Administrative Procedure Act notice-and-comment window is exposed to State Farm arbitrary-and-capricious review the moment a denied or delayed deployment lands in the DC Circuit. Senators Mark Warner and Todd Young jointly request a classified NIST plus ODNI cyber-lead briefing on the threshold methodology, tentatively scheduled for May 15 before any final EO signs. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind hold the cohort consensus from the May 7 reciprocity protocol with statements supporting a comment window in principle while declining to oppose the Section 708 vehicle.

items.headline: Singapore IMDA and Japan AISI sign Indo-Pacific cyber-eval reciprocity memorandum
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's EU-UK joint cyber-eval reciprocity protocol stood alone as the multilateral primitive. Today, within 24 hours, Singapore IMDA and Japan AISI publish a parallel memorandum-of-cooperation accepting AISI-administered TLO-range cyber-evaluation runs as satisfying their respective frontier-model voluntary-disclosure regimes with a 120-day placement window. Canada CCCS and Australia ASD ACSC sign on as observers and pre-commit to mirror language by Q3 2026. The Singapore-Japan memorandum explicitly cites the May 7 EU-UK protocol as its template and the Mythos and GPT-5.5 results as the operational threshold. A four-jurisdiction recognition perimeter is now visible inside one news cycle, sharpening US absence from the cyber-eval reciprocity layer as the FMRB drafting continues.

items.headline: UK NCSC sovereign procurement freeze hits named-vendor scope
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's UK action was a one-week procurement pause and a CNI advisory expansion across DWP, HMRC, and Network Rail. Today NHS Digital, DWP, and HMRC each publish revised May 15 maintainer-facing repository-lockdown lists, with HMRC alone walling off 327 internal repositories and DWP at 196. HM Treasury extends the LLM-coding-assistant procurement pause from one week to a 30-day formal review and adds Google Gemini Code Assist plus Microsoft GitHub Copilot for Government tenants to a temporarily-suspended-vendors annex pending Mythos-class capability disclosure under the AI Procurement Common Standard. Cabinet Office requests written submissions from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft by May 22 on offensive-cyber-capability test results conducted against UK-public-sector source-code estates. The first sovereign procurement freeze with named-vendor scope lands.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS opens 18.3 percent above IPO price on Nasdaq debut
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Cerebras priced at $128, three dollars above the upper end of range, with $4.12B raised including the green-shoe and a $27.2B fully-diluted market cap. Today CBRS opens at $151.40 on Nasdaq, +18.3% over the IPO price, briefly touches $158.20 intraday, settles near $148 at close on roughly 28M shares, and lands a fully-diluted market cap near $31.4B, beating the original $26.6B target by about 18%. OpenAI's $1B warrant package marks at roughly $4.9B paper gain at close. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Citi initiate Buy ratings with $165 to $185 12-month price targets explicitly citing the OpenAI 1GW first-data-center commitment and the still-undisclosed Saudi Aramco Digital MoU as upside drivers. The first-day pop becomes the operative reference for the SambaNova, Groq, and Tenstorrent S-1 cohort.

items.headline: SEC Corp Fin opens AI-services-revenue inquiry letter cycle
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's hyperscaler thread closed on Microsoft's $52B annualized Azure AI Services run-rate disclosure with a CFO commitment to a Q4 AI-services 10-Q footnote breakout starting fiscal Q1-2027. Today SEC Corporation Finance staff posts a sample comment letter to its frequently-requested-comment-letters page asking Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta to clarify their AI-services-revenue measurement basis, capital-allocation attribution, and customer-concentration footnote schedule for the upcoming Q2 10-Q. The letter explicitly references the OpenAI Cerebras warrant package as a comparable for related-party-disclosure exhibit treatment. Sell-side desks lift their AI-services 10-Q footnote breakout probability for the Q1 2027 fiscal-cycle landing toward the high end. Alphabet analyst day moves to May 21 with Gemini training-cluster cost-of-revenue confirmed as a segment-discussion topic.

items.headline: Nvidia and AMD pre-announce supply-allocation guidance via dual 8-Ks
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday AMD's Helios plus MI450 H2-2026 commitments named six of the top ten hyperscaler and neocloud accounts via investor-day commentary, while Nvidia's Vera Rubin sampling cadence and NVL576 H1-2027 disclosure lived in a SEMICON West side-meeting and an investor letter. Today both companies harden the disclosure into 8-K filings: Nvidia confirms Vera Rubin sampling has reached production-volume customer commitments for nine of the top ten hyperscaler and neocloud accounts with NVL576 H1-2027 backlog now covered through Q3 2027 at current Blackwell B200 cadence (~1,000 NVL72 racks/week); AMD lifts the disclosed Helios plus MI450 commitment book to 6.2GW total across Microsoft Azure, Oracle, OpenAI, Crusoe, CoreWeave, and Lambda, plus a previously-undisclosed 0.8GW Tencent Cloud commitment for Asia-Pacific deployment. The dual 8-Ks crystallize the duopoly forward-cadence record on file.

items.headline: Ni8mare day-eight scan shows 41.5% drop in exposed instances post-KEV
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Shadowserver's first-week scan found roughly 14,200 internet-exposed n8n instances pre-1.121.0 globally with about 62% unpatched at the moment of CISA KEV catalog addition. Today the day-eight scan drops the count from ~14,200 to ~8,300 (-41.5% in 24 hours following KEV listing) with the steepest drops in Germany (1,920 to 980) and France (880 to 410), and roughly 47% of remaining exposed instances still unpatched. Censys honeypot telemetry observes a 4.8x spike in exploitation attempts on the n8n REST webhook entry point during the first 12 hours after KEV listing, consistent with opportunistic scanning by commodity-tier exploit kits incorporating the proof-of-concept. NHS England issues a separate emergency advisory naming Ni8mare among an enumerated list of agentic-AI workflow-platform CVEs that block migration into the NHS Federated Data Platform technology estate.

items.headline: CrewAI and Haystack CVEs continue weekly agentic-platform disclosure cadence
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's LangGraph SSRF (CVE-2026-44012) plus LiteLLM auth-bypass (CVE-2026-44188) pair was the day's confirmation that agentic-platform CVE disclosures had moved to multi-vendor weekly cadence. Today, exactly 24 hours later, two more land: CrewAI CVE-2026-44352 (CVSS 8.7) is a deserialization vulnerability in the agent-task-checkpoint loader allowing arbitrary code execution by a malicious checkpoint file uploaded via connected RAG storage (patched in v0.118.2 same-day); Haystack CVE-2026-44391 (CVSS 9.4) is an unauthenticated path-traversal in the deepset-cloud agent-tool registry permitting attacker-controlled file reads and pivot to AWS instance-metadata endpoints (patched in v2.21.4). A joint Aikido and Sysdig write-up estimates the broader open-source agentic-orchestrator codebase contains a structurally similar exposure pattern across at least seven additional unmaintained agent-checkpoint loaders. Multi-vendor weekly cadence is now confirmed.

items.headline: Microsoft Defender MCP module quarantines 19% of net-new servers in first 30 minutes
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's MCP-server attack-surface telemetry placed exposed-server count at ~9,400, up from ~7,000 in the early-May baseline (+34% in 4 weeks), with Microsoft Defender for Cloud's MCP-server threat-detection module just GA. Today the third weekly update places exposed servers at ~10,400 (+10.6% week-on-week) with growth visibly slowing as the Defender module takes effect: 19% of net-new MCP servers seen on Defender-protected estates were quarantined within their first 30 minutes versus the unprotected baseline. Cisco Astrix Security, freshly closed May 4, ships a co-branded MCP-server identity gateway integrating with the Defender XDR feed plus the Microsoft Agent 365 audit ledger. The combined telemetry layer is the first cross-vendor agentic-AI control-plane stack with data-plane visibility on more than 60% of new MCP-server provisioning events.

items.headline: Three hyperscalers ship managed agent-registry tiers within 24 hours
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 and OpenAI's per-org agent registry landed as the dual frontier-lab governance-by-design answer to the agentic-AI attack-surface concern. Today Microsoft Azure AI Foundry announces a managed Skill Catalog with signed-skill registration, version-pinning, and per-tenant capability gating that integrates with Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 plus OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise; AWS Bedrock announces an Agent Registry preview with FedRAMP-Moderate inheritance from the Bedrock Government partition; Google Cloud Vertex AI announces Agent Governance Center entering public preview with an expanded model-card schema covering signed-skill provenance plus per-tenant Mythos-class gating. Three-vendor parallel hyperscaler landing inside 24 hours pulls the May 7 frontier-lab registry shape into the hyperscaler procurement perimeter ahead of the Q4 2026 enterprise-RFP cycle.

items.headline: Mistral Workflows tenancy crosses 290 customers with Codestral CLI integration
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday paid Workflows tenancy crossed 240 enterprise customers and 3.4M daily executions on the Capgemini, Atos, and EDF go-lives one week post-preview. Today Mistral discloses three additional go-lives: BNP Paribas Securities Services launches a Workflows-orchestrated trade-confirmation reconciliation agent across European custody operations; Siemens Healthineers ships a Workflows-managed clinical-trial-protocol document review agent across 14 EU sites; Saudi Aramco Digital announces a sovereign-cloud Workflows deployment for upstream-asset-integrity inspection routing across Aramco refinery and petrochemical complexes. Paid Workflows tenancy crosses 290 enterprise customers with daily-execution count surpassing 4.1M. Mistral simultaneously announces a Workflows-Codestral integration that lets developers iterate workflow definitions inside the Codestral CLI with explicit per-step token-budget bookkeeping, mirroring the OpenAI Codex CLI Plan-Apply mode shipped May 7.

items.headline: Claude Code 3.0 day-one telemetry shows 11,400 skills and 612K installs
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Anthropic shipped Claude Code 3.0 with the sandboxed-skill registry, per-tenant Mythos Preview gating, and a contractual ethics-and-misuse rider as the structural answer to the agentic-AI attack-surface concern. Today Anthropic publishes day-one telemetry: 11,400 skills published and 612K skill installs in the first 24 hours, with 87% of skills installed via the per-tenant capability-gating workflow rather than ad-hoc copy-paste. Per-tenant Mythos Preview gating is enabled by 38 enterprise customers including JPMorgan Chase, Booz Allen Hamilton, Mandiant Consulting, and Raytheon under the new contractual rider. Project Glasswing telemetry feeds into the registry's quarantine-evidence dashboard, with 14 Mythos-class skills auto-quarantined day-one for failing the per-tenant capability gate. Simon Willison's annotation cites the registry's signed-version pinning as the structural answer to the agent-skills attack-surface concern raised earlier in April.

items.headline: Unsloth router-only LoRA arxiv paper extends evaluation to four MoE models
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Unsloth's router-only LoRA training mode shipped with vendor benchmarks reporting 73% of full-LoRA-on-experts accuracy at 8.4% of training-step time and 12% of peak VRAM on Qwen3.6-Max alone. Today the arxiv preprint Router-Only LoRA for Mixture-of-Experts Models, jointly authored with Hugging Face, presents the formal evaluation across Qwen3.6-Max, Mixtral 8x22B, DBRX, and Kimi K2.6, reporting 71-78% of full-LoRA-on-experts accuracy at 8-13% of training-step time and 11-16% of peak VRAM. New recipes ship for Llama 4 Behemoth-class router-only tuning (target H100 plus B200 single-node), Kimi K2.6 router-only on RTX 6000 Ada workstation tier (96GB VRAM), and Mixtral 8x22B router-only adaptation for sovereign-cloud customers requiring no Hugging Face dependency at inference time. DeepMind's same-day arxiv paper on router-aware advantage decomposition closes the long-context training-stability gap that previously blocked router-only mode for ultra-long-context Reinforcement Learning.

items.headline: vLLM v0.11.1 and SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 ship security and performance follow-ups
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday vLLM v0.11 closed the H100 throughput gap to SGLang from 29% to 14% on shared-prefix workloads with a RadixAttention-compatible prefix-cache. Today vLLM v0.11.1 patches a CVSS 7.4 prefix-cache poisoning issue (CVE-2026-44512, cross-tenant prefix-cache key collision under multi-tenant deployment) and adds a disaggregated-prefill mode mirroring Cloudflare Infire's edge architecture. SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 ships a 2.1x speedup on tool-calling-heavy agentic workloads via RadixAttention-aware tool-result-cache reuse plus a CVSS 8.1 fix for an authenticated server-side template injection (CVE-2026-44567) discovered by Trail of Bits during a post-Cerebras IPO inference-stack red-team sweep. The Yotta Labs benchmark refresh now places vLLM at ~14,650 tok/s and SGLang RadixArk at ~17,300 tok/s, narrowing the gap to 15.3% at the H100 tier.

items.headline: Cerebras CS-4 engineering sample lands on IPO trading-debut day
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's hardware narrative was anchored by the AMD Helios H2-2026 commitments and the Nvidia Vera Rubin sampling disclosure, with no Cerebras roadmap update past the IPO pricing. Today Cerebras unveils the next-generation CS-4 wafer-scale engine with 1.2x the on-wafer SRAM, an upgraded 6.4Tb/s SwarmX fabric for cross-system clustering, and a published peak training throughput of 71 PFLOPS dense BF16 versus CS-3's 56 PFLOPS, with first customer engineering-sample shipments targeted for Q1 2027. OpenAI confirms its standing $10B multi-year supply agreement covers CS-4 deliveries inside the second-data-center commitment announced earlier in the year. Cerebras CTO comments that CS-4 specifically targets Mixture-of-Experts router-only training plus ultra-long-context Reinforcement Learning workloads, citing the same-morning Unsloth and Hugging Face joint preprint. Pairs with the Nvidia Vera Rubin and AMD Helios H2-2026 cadence to crystallize the three-vendor AI-accelerator roadmap.

items.headline: Tenstorrent ships first Wormhole Galaxy production rack with IPO bridge closed
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Tenstorrent appeared in the post-Cerebras IPO follow-on coverage as a late-stage discussion participant with Hyundai and Samsung Foundry on a >$3B IPO bridge round. Today Tenstorrent announces general availability of its Galaxy rack, configured with 32 Wormhole-derived Quasar n300 boards (8,192 RISC-V Tensix cores plus 16 ARM A-class management cores) targeting inference-throughput-optimized open-architecture workloads, with first customers CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, and Crusoe, and Hyundai's Robotics Metaplant Application Center adopting Galaxy for on-prem humanoid policy fine-tuning and inference. Jim Keller confirms the $3.4B IPO bridge round with Hyundai and Samsung Foundry as co-anchors closed Wednesday, with a confidential S-1 submission targeted for July. The third independent AI-accelerator vendor with shipping production hardware in 2026 lands.

items.headline: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 production pulls in two months and adds Stellantis pilot
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's humanoid league-table thesis crystallized on the Figure 03 BMW Spartanburg 14-day production-run record plus the Apptronik Apollo Mercedes Sindelfingen 6-to-36 expansion, with Tesla Optimus Gen 3 still tracking a late-July to August Fremont start. Today Tesla files an 8-K confirming low-volume Optimus Gen 3 production has commenced at the Fremont pilot line two months ahead of that window, with first 240 units allocated for internal Gigafactory Texas plus Fremont automotive-line cell-pickup and torque-fastening tasks plus 60 units for a previously-undisclosed Stellantis Detroit pilot beginning in late June. Tesla maintains the 10M-units-per-year long-run target at the Gigafactory Texas 5.2M sq ft Optimus factory expansion. The IROS / GTC Fall 2026 humanoid league-table now has four production-line entries with hard MTBF disclosures.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai expand Atlas commercial roster across three sectors
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's Physical AI thread did not extend the Atlas commercial deployment beyond the standing Boston Dynamics commercial-production launch reference. Today Hyundai's Robotics Metaplant Application Center confirms a 60-unit Atlas commercial deployment at Hyundai Steel's Dangjin Works for hot-rolled-coil handling and a 24-unit deployment at Kia's Slovak Zilina plant for paint-line subassembly, while Boston Dynamics simultaneously announces an Atlas pilot at LG Energy Solution's Holland Michigan battery plant for cell-stacking quality-inspection. The Atlas commercial roster now spans automotive (Hyundai, Kia), heavy-industry (Hyundai Steel), and battery manufacturing (LG Energy Solution) inside a single quarter, with Boston Dynamics reporting a 2.6x average per-unit MTBF improvement across pilot-to-production transitions. Atlas continues selling at the cited $140K-plus enterprise tier vs Optimus's $20K-$30K consumer-target range.

items.headline: DeepMind router-aware advantage decomposition paper extends arxiv RL wave
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's arxiv wave covered verifier-free process rewards, multi-agent cooperative search trees, and inference-time compute routing as three concurrent papers maintaining the RL-reward, multi-agent, and SLM-routing convergence thesis. Today three new preprints extend each of those threads at scale: Self-Generated Process Critiques at Scale (2605.05702) reports 6.4-9.1% absolute gain on math-reasoning benchmarks across 13B and 70B base models while removing all human-annotated process-reward labels; Cooperative Search Trees with Role-Asymmetric Agents (2605.05789) provides the proof-of-correctness companion formalizing convergence guarantees; Adaptive Inference Compute Routing for Mixture of Specialists Across Trust Boundaries (2605.05821) extends the routing paper with a security-aware variant respecting per-tenant capability-gating boundaries (the Project Glasswing primitive), reporting 41% inference-cost reduction with formal no-cross-tenant-leakage guarantees. DeepMind separately publishes Stable Long-Context Reinforcement Learning via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition (2605.05844), directly relevant to the same-day Unsloth router-only LoRA recipes.
